 THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 11.10.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO.227/2019 ON THE FILE OF THE PRL. SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM, MACT,
KOLAR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2024:KHC:20600  MFA No. 178 of 2022  C/W MFA No. 215 of 2022  JUDGMENT M.F.A. No.178/2022 has been filed by the claimant in MVC No.230/2019 and M.F.A. No.215/2022 has been filed by the claimant in MVC No.227/2019.

Both the appeals have been filed against the judgment and award dated 11.10.2021 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kolar, seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
The case of the petitioners is that they filed the claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in the road traffic accident that occurred on 30.08.2019 at 1.35 PM at Mulbagal-Kolar NH.75 Road, Nallur Gate,
Mulbagal Taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing No.KA-51- MA-4295.

It is alleged that the petitioners were proceeding to their village and when they reached Nallur Gate, at that time, NC: 2024:KHC:20600 the offending vehicle came from Mulabagal in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the claimants.
On account of the same, the petitioners sustained injuries.

One person died in the accident, whose legal heirs have filed a separate claim petition in MVC No.226/2019.
5.
The respondent-insurance company filed the statement of objections denying the accident, age and income and occupation of the injured and prayed for dismissal of the claim petitions.

6. Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following common issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that she/he sustained grievous injuries due to road traffic accident occurred on 30.08.2019 at 1.35 PM at Mulbagal-Kolar NH.75 Road,
Nalluru Gate, Mulbagal Taluk, due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-MA-4295?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, from whom and how much ?
3.
For what order or award ?
The petitioner in MVC No.230/2019 was examined as P.W.1 and the petitioner in MVC No.227/2019 was examined as P.W.2 and got marked 22 documents.

On behalf of respondent, the Manager of respondent was examined as R.W.1 and 10 documents were got marked.
8.
After hearing the arguments of the learned counsel for the parties, the Tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- as global compensation to each of the petitioners, which is under challenge.

9. Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the petitioner in MVC No.227/2019 has sustained almost four injuries and was admitted in the hospital for three days, but the Tribunal,
without considering the said fact, has granted the global compensation of Rs.15,000/- which is not correct.

There is no amount awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, medical expenses,
food and nourishment and conveyance charges, etc.
Therefore, prayed for allowing the appeal.

The learned counsel for the petitioner in MVC No.230/2019 has also argued on par with the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner in MVC No.227/2019 and accordingly, prayed Anjappa vs Kiran Kumar .C on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169685809/
4 for allowing the appeal.

11. On the contrary, the learned counsel the respondent- insurance company has supported the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and contended that the injuries suffered by the petitioners are simple in nature and therefore, the Tribunal has granted the just compensation,
which does not require any interference, and therefore, prayed for dismissal of the appeals.
12. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the records.
13. Perusal of the records indicates the clear error committed by the Tribunal in awarding Rs.15,000/- each to the petitioners, which is meager compensation and it requires enhancement.

The evidence of the petitioner in MVC No.227/2019 (appellant in M.F.A. No.215/2022) and the documents produced therein, reveals that the petitioner sustained injury on the head, right forearm and injuries on the back bone.
The wound certificate-Ex.P.18 indicates the same.
Ex.P.19 is medical bill worth Rs.5,408/-.
As per the discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to the hospital for three days.
Though the petitioner sustained injuries, as aforesaid, and they are simple in nature, but she was admitted in the hospital for three days for the injuries sustained by her.

Such being the case,
awarding global compensation of Rs.15,000/- by the Tribunal, is not correct.
Therefore, on that ground, this Court grants Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering.
15. As regards the medical expenses, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,408/- and she was admitted in the hospital for three days.
Therefore, definitely, she might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment, attendant charges, conveyance, etc.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head food and nourishment, attendant NC: 2024:KHC:20600 charges,
conveyance, etc. and the petitioner is also entitled for Rs.5,500/- towards medical expenses.
16. The doctor has not been examined by the petitioner and there is no bill submitted by the petitioner.
Such being the case, the petitioner is not entitled for any other compensation.

Therefore,
the petitioner is awarded Rs.50,500/- as compensation.
17. In respect of the appellant in M.F.A. No.178/2022 (the petitioner in MVC No.230/2019), he has been awarded Rs.15,000/- as global compensation by the Tribunal, which is also incorrect.
The petitioner himself has produced the documents at Ex.P.14-discharge summary and Ex.P.15-wounds certificate.
As per the discharge summary, the petitioner has sustained lacerated injury over the back and abrasion over the right shoulder.
The doctor has given the discharge certificate wherein it is stated that the petitioner sustained injury to right frontal, right shoulder and the left elbow.
Therefore, granting the global compensation of Rs.15,000/- by the Tribunal is not correct.

Therefore, this Court grants the compensation of - 10 - Anjappa vs Kiran Kumar .C on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169685809/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:20600 Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering.
The petitioner was also admitted in the hospital for three days from 30.08.2019 to 01.09.2019 and also spent Rs.5,639/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,000/- towards the medical expenses.

The petitioner is also granted Rs.20,000/- towards food, nourishment and attendant charges, etc.
because the petitioner had severe injuries and he might have spent some amount towards the attendant charges, nourishment and food, when he got admitted in the hospital.

Therefore, in all,
the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.51,000/-.
18.
